Human: Generate a complete medium-size Java 11 repository architecture for: 2048 game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: pom.xml
- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.


Project-specific Java correctness contract:
- Board is the sole owner of one authoritative 4x4 int grid; getGridCopy() returns a deep read-only snapshot, so Game and spawners must never try to mutate the board through getGridCopy()
- declare one exact mutation API void setCell(int row, int col, int value) with bounds checks and 0-or-power-of-two validation, and use it consistently for deterministic setup and applying every Spawn; do not invent setGridValue, placeTile, setTile, or aliases
- declare boolean hasTileAtLeast(int value) on Board and use that exact name for win detection; do not invent hasValueAtLeast or aliases
- declare a simple immutable MoveResult with exact accessors boolean changed() and int scoreGained(); Board.move(Direction) returns it, and Game must use these methods rather than fields
- Board.move must implement each row/column by reading exactly four values in movement order, compacting nonzero values, merging one equal adjacent pair at most once, compacting/filling with zero, writing all four results back to the authoritative grid, and summing each newly merged tile into scoreGained; forbid generic multi-delta helpers with unused or ambiguous row/column parameters
- Game.move(Direction) calls Board.move once, adds scoreGained, and spawns exactly one tile only when changed() is true; apply the Spawn via Board.setCell, never via a copied array
- Game must update status after every move attempt, including an unchanged move: WON iff Board.hasTileAtLeast(2048), otherwise LOST iff !Board.hasAnyMoves(), otherwise IN_PROGRESS
- initialization/reset must clear the authoritative Board and apply exactly two spawns through Board.setCell; a deterministic SequenceSpawner must consume its documented sequence in order
- keep MainTest to 2--4 concise deterministic tests using only the canonical methods; do not assert mutations made to arrays returned by getGridCopy()
- repeat the exact getGridCopy immutability, setCell, hasTileAtLeast, MoveResult, line-merge, spawn-on-change, and status-transition rules in Full API specification, Logic Analysis, Shared Knowledge, and every affected implementation task; vague descriptions are insufficient


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 7 repository files
- about 33 functions or methods
- about 650 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- 4x4 board
- left right up and down moves
- single-merge-per-move rule
- score accumulation
- deterministic tile spawning
- win loss and reset states

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Generate a complete medium-size Java 11 repository architecture for: 2048 game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: pom.xml
- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.


Project-specific Java correctness contract:
- Board is the sole owner of one authoritative 4x4 int grid; getGridCopy() returns a deep read-only snapshot, so Game and spawners must never try to mutate the board through getGridCopy()
- declare one exact mutation API void setCell(int row, int col, int value) with bounds checks and 0-or-power-of-two validation, and use it consistently for deterministic setup and applying every Spawn; do not invent setGridValue, placeTile, setTile, or aliases
- declare boolean hasTileAtLeast(int value) on Board and use that exact name for win detection; do not invent hasValueAtLeast or aliases
- declare a simple immutable MoveResult with exact accessors boolean changed() and int scoreGained(); Board.move(Direction) returns it, and Game must use these methods rather than fields
- Board.move must implement each row/column by reading exactly four values in movement order, compacting nonzero values, merging one equal adjacent pair at most once, compacting/filling with zero, writing all four results back to the authoritative grid, and summing each newly merged tile into scoreGained; forbid generic multi-delta helpers with unused or ambiguous row/column parameters
- Game.move(Direction) calls Board.move once, adds scoreGained, and spawns exactly one tile only when changed() is true; apply the Spawn via Board.setCell, never via a copied array
- Game must update status after every move attempt, including an unchanged move: WON iff Board.hasTileAtLeast(2048), otherwise LOST iff !Board.hasAnyMoves(), otherwise IN_PROGRESS
- initialization/reset must clear the authoritative Board and apply exactly two spawns through Board.setCell; a deterministic SequenceSpawner must consume its documented sequence in order
- keep MainTest to 2--4 concise deterministic tests using only the canonical methods; do not assert mutations made to arrays returned by getGridCopy()
- repeat the exact getGridCopy immutability, setCell, hasTileAtLeast, MoveResult, line-merge, spawn-on-change, and status-transition rules in Full API specification, Logic Analysis, Shared Knowledge, and every affected implementation task; vague descriptions are insufficient


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 7 repository files
- about 33 functions or methods
- about 650 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- 4x4 board
- left right up and down moves
- single-merge-per-move rule
- score accumulation
- deterministic tile spawning
- win loss and reset states

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Implementations must not return null.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/SequenceSpawner.java:\\n- public final class SequenceSpawner implements Spawner { public SequenceSpawner(java.util.List<Spawn> seq); public Spawn nextSpawn(); public static SequenceSpawner defaultSequence(); }\\n- Holds an ordered sequence of Spawn. nextSpawn() returns sequence[index] and advances index; when reaching end, wraps to start and continues. defaultSequence() returns a deterministic spawner with a documented sequence; the first two spawns are used by Game.reset().\\n\\nsrc/main/java/GameStatus.java:\\n- public enum GameStatus { IN_PROGRESS, WON, LOST }\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Board.java:\\n- public final class Board {\\n  public Board();\\n  public void clear();\\n  public int[][] getGridCopy();\\n  public void setCell(int row, int col, int value);\\n  public MoveResult move(Direction dir);\\n  public boolean hasTileAtLeast(int value);\\n  public boolean hasAnyMoves();\\n}\\nSemantics:\\n- Board owns the authoritative 4x4 int grid. No external code may mutate it except through setCell().\\n- getGridCopy() returns a deep snapshot (new arrays). Callers must not mutate the returned arrays expecting to affect Board.\\n- setCell(row,col,value) performs bounds checks (0..3) and value validation: value == 0 or value is a positive power of two. Sets grid[row][col] accordingly.\\n- move(dir) processes each of the four lines (rows for LEFT/RIGHT, columns for UP/DOWN) independently:\\n  * Read exactly four values in movement order (LEFT: left->right; RIGHT: right->left; UP: top->bottom; DOWN: bottom->top).\\n  * Compact nonzero tiles preserving order.\\n  * Merge adjacent equal tiles at most once per adjacency (i.e., a tile participates in at most one merge). When merging two equal tiles x and x, produce 2x and add 2x to scoreGained.\\n  * After merging, compact again and fill with zeros to length four.\\n  * Write back exactly four results to the grid in the same line and movement orientation.\\n  * Overall changed flag is true if any cell differs from its previous value anywhere on the grid.\\n- hasTileAtLeast(value) returns true if any cell >= value.\\n- hasAnyMoves() returns true if any cell is zero, or any horizontal or vertical adjacent pair is equal, implying at least one legal move remains.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Game.java:\\n- public final class Game {\\n  public Game(Board board, Spawner spawner);\\n  public void reset();\\n  public MoveResult move(Direction dir);\\n  public int getScore();\\n  public GameStatus getStatus();\\n  public int[][] getGridCopy();\\n}\\nSemantics:\\n- Constructor requires non-null Board and Spawner; initializes score to 0 and status to IN_PROGRESS.\\n- reset(): calls board.clear() and applies exactly two spawns, each obtained by spawner.nextSpawn() and applied via board.setCell(). Resets score to 0 and status to IN_PROGRESS.\\n- move(dir): calls board.move(dir) once, increments internal score by result.scoreGained(). If result.changed() is true, consumes exactly one Spawn from spawner and applies it via board.setCell(). After the move attempt (even if unchanged), updates status: WON iff board.hasTileAtLeast(2048); else LOST iff !board.hasAnyMoves(); else IN_PROGRESS. Public API and semantics:\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Direction.java: public enum Direction { LEFT, RIGHT, UP, DOWN }\\n- Used by Board.move(Direction) and Game.move(Direction).\\n\\nsrc/main/java/MoveResult.java:\\n- public final class MoveResult { public MoveResult(boolean changed, int scoreGained); public boolean changed(); public int scoreGained(); }\\n- Immutable: fields set at construction and never change. changed() indicates whether any grid cell changed. scoreGained() sums all newly created tile values from merges performed by that single move.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Spawn.java:\\n- public final class Spawn { public Spawn(int row, int col, int value); public int row(); public int col(); public int value(); }\\n- Constructor validates: 0 <= row < 4, 0 <= col < 4, value > 0 and a power of two (e.g., 2,4,8,...). Immutable.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Spawner.java:\\n- public interface Spawner { Spawn nextSpawn(); }\\n- Contract: Deterministic source. Game consumes exactly two spawns during reset() and exactly one spawn after a changed move. Implementations must not return null.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/SequenceSpawner.java:\\n- public final class SequenceSpawner implements Spawner { public SequenceSpawner(java.util.List<Spawn> seq); public Spawn nextSpawn(); public static SequenceSpawner defaultSequence(); }\\n- Holds an ordered sequence of Spawn. nextSpawn() returns sequence[index] and advances index; when reaching end, wraps to start and continues. defaultSequence() returns a deterministic spawner with a documented sequence; the first two spawns are used by Game.reset().\\n\\nsrc/main/java/GameStatus.java:\\n- public enum GameStatus { IN_PROGRESS, WON, LOST }\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Board.java:\\n- public final class Board {\\n  public Board();\\n  public void clear();\\n  public int[][] getGridCopy();\\n  public void setCell(int row, int col, int value);\\n  public MoveResult move(Direction dir);\\n  public boolean hasTileAtLeast(int value);\\n  public boolean hasAnyMoves();\\n}\\nSemantics:\\n- Board owns the authoritative 4x4 int grid. No external code may mutate it except through setCell().\\n- getGridCopy() returns a deep snapshot (new arrays). Callers must not mutate the returned arrays expecting to affect Board.\\n- setCell(row,col,value) performs bounds checks (0..3) and value validation: value == 0 or value is a positive power of two. Sets grid[row][col] accordingly.\\n- move(dir) processes each of the four lines (rows for LEFT/RIGHT, columns for UP/DOWN) independently:\\n  * Read exactly four values in movement order (LEFT: left->right; RIGHT: right->left; UP: top->bottom; DOWN: bottom->top).\\n  * Compact nonzero tiles preserving order.\\n  * Merge adjacent equal tiles at most once per adjacency (i.e., a tile participates in at most one merge). When merging two equal tiles x and x, produce 2x and add 2x to scoreGained.\\n  * After merging, compact again and fill with zeros to length four.\\n  * Write back exactly four results to the grid in the same line and movement orientation.\\n  * Overall changed flag is true if any cell differs from its previous value anywhere on the grid.\\n- hasTileAtLeast(value) returns true if any cell >= value.\\n- hasAnyMoves() returns true if any cell is zero, or any horizontal or vertical adjacent pair is equal, implying at least one legal move remains.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Game.java:\\n- public final class Game {\\n  public Game(Board board, Spawner spawner);\\n  public void reset();\\n  public MoveResult move(Direction dir);\\n  public int getScore();\\n  public GameStatus getStatus();\\n  public int[][] getGridCopy();\\n}\\nSemantics:\\n- Constructor requires non-null Board and Spawner; initializes score to 0 and status to IN_PROGRESS.\\n- reset(): calls board.clear() and applies exactly two spawns, each obtained by spawner.nextSpawn() and applied via board.setCell(). Resets score to 0 and status to IN_PROGRESS.\\n- move(dir): calls board.move(dir) once, increments internal score by result.scoreGained(). If result.changed() is true, consumes exactly one Spawn from spawner and applies it via board.setCell(). After the move attempt (even if unchanged), updates status: WON iff board.hasTileAtLeast(2048); else LOST iff !board.hasAnyMoves(); else IN_PROGRESS. Returns the MoveResult from Board.\\n- getGridCopy() proxies board.getGridCopy().\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Main.java:\\n- public final class Main { public static void main(String[] args); }\\n- Deterministic headless console demo: constructs SequenceSpawner.defaultSequence(), Board, Game; calls reset(); performs one move (e.g., Direction.LEFT); prints the 4x4 grid, current score, and status in a plain text format; exits.\\n\\nBuild & Test:\\n- pom.xml sets Java 11, includes JUnit Jupiter as test dependency, and a Surefire plugin version supporting JUnit 5. No external non-test dependencies.\\n\\nImport/Dependency rules:\\n- Board is the sole owner of the grid. All mutations go through Board.setCell().\\n- Pure domain logic (Board, MoveResult, Direction, Spawner, SequenceSpawner, Spawn, GameStatus, Game) must not depend on environment-specific code (Main). Main depends on Game and related domain classes only.\\n- Tests use JUnit 5 (Jupiter) and reference only declared classes.\\n\\nDeterminism:\\n- SequenceSpawner consumes its sequence strictly in order for both reset() and subsequent spawns.\",\"Shared Knowledge\":\"Protocol files: pom.xml, src/main/java/Main.java (entry), and src/test/java/MainTest.java (single test) are preserved exactly. Public API and semantics:\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Direction.java: public enum Direction { LEFT, RIGHT, UP, DOWN }\\n- Used by Board.move(Direction) and Game.move(Direction).\\n\\nsrc/main/java/MoveResult.java:\\n- public final class MoveResult { public MoveResult(boolean changed, int scoreGained); public boolean changed(); public int scoreGained(); }\\n- Immutable: fields set at construction and never change. changed() indicates whether any grid cell changed. scoreGained() sums all newly created tile values from merges performed by that single move.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Spawn.java:\\n- public final class Spawn { public Spawn(int row, int col, int value); public int row(); public int col(); public int value(); }\\n- Constructor validates: 0 <= row < 4, 0 <= col < 4, value > 0 and a power of two (e.g., 2,4,8,...). Immutable.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Spawner.java:\\n- public interface Spawner { Spawn nextSpawn(); }\\n- Contract: Deterministic source. Game consumes exactly two spawns during reset() and exactly one spawn after a changed move. Implementations must not return null.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/SequenceSpawner.java:\\n- public final class SequenceSpawner implements Spawner { public SequenceSpawner(java.util.List<Spawn> seq); public Spawn nextSpawn(); public static SequenceSpawner defaultSequence(); }\\n- Holds an ordered sequence of Spawn. nextSpawn() returns sequence[index] and advances index; when reaching end, wraps to start and continues. defaultSequence() returns a deterministic spawner with a documented sequence; the first two spawns are used by Game.reset().\\n\\nsrc/main/java/GameStatus.java:\\n- public enum GameStatus { IN_PROGRESS, WON, LOST }\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Board.java:\\n- public final class Board {\\n  public Board();\\n  public void clear();\\n  public int[][] getGridCopy();\\n  public void setCell(int row, int col, int value);\\n  public MoveResult move(Direction dir);\\n  public boolean hasTileAtLeast(int value);\\n  public boolean hasAnyMoves();\\n}\\nSemantics:\\n- Board owns the authoritative 4x4 int grid. No external code may mutate it except through setCell().\\n- getGridCopy() returns a deep snapshot (new arrays). Callers must not mutate the returned arrays expecting to affect Board.\\n- setCell(row,col,value) performs bounds checks (0..3) and value validation: value == 0 or value is a positive power of two. Sets grid[row][col] accordingly.\\n- move(dir) processes each of the four lines (rows for LEFT/RIGHT, columns for UP/DOWN) independently:\\n  * Read exactly four values in movement order (LEFT: left->right; RIGHT: right->left; UP: top->bottom; DOWN: bottom->top).\\n  * Compact nonzero tiles preserving order.\\n  * Merge adjacent equal tiles at most once per adjacency (i.e., a tile participates in at most one merge). When merging two equal tiles x and x, produce 2x and add 2x to scoreGained.\\n  * After merging, compact again and fill with zeros to length four.\\n  * Write back exactly four results to the grid in the same line and movement orientation.\\n  * Overall changed flag is true if any cell differs from its previous value anywhere on the grid.\\n- hasTileAtLeast(value) returns true if any cell >= value.\\n- hasAnyMoves() returns true if any cell is zero, or any horizontal or vertical adjacent pair is equal, implying at least one legal move remains.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Game.java:\\n- public final class Game {\\n  public Game(Board board, Spawner spawner);\\n  public void reset();\\n  public MoveResult move(Direction dir);\\n  public int getScore();\\n  public GameStatus getStatus();\\n  public int[][] getGridCopy();\\n}\\nSemantics:\\n- Constructor requires non-null Board and Spawner; initializes score to 0 and status to IN_PROGRESS.\\n- reset(): calls board.clear() and applies exactly two spawns, each obtained by spawner.nextSpawn() and applied via board.setCell(). Resets score to 0 and status to IN_PROGRESS.\\n- move(dir): calls board.move(dir) once, increments internal score by result.scoreGained(). If result.changed() is true, consumes exactly one Spawn from spawner and applies it via board.setCell(). After the move attempt (even if unchanged), updates status: WON iff board.hasTileAtLeast(2048); else LOST iff !board.hasAnyMoves(); else IN_PROGRESS. Returns the MoveResult from Board.\\n- getGridCopy() proxies board.getGridCopy().\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Main.java:\\n- public final class Main { public static void main(String[] args); }\\n- Deterministic headless console demo: constructs SequenceSpawner.defaultSequence(), Board, Game; calls reset(); performs one move (e.g., Direction.LEFT); prints the 4x4 grid, current score, and status in a plain text format; exits.\\n\\nBuild & Test:\\n- pom.xml sets Java 11, includes JUnit Jupiter as test dependency, and a Surefire plugin version supporting JUnit 5. No external non-test dependencies.\\n\\nImport/Dependency rules:\\n- Board is the sole owner of the grid. All mutations go through Board.setCell().\\n- Pure domain logic (Board, MoveResult, Direction, Spawner, SequenceSpawner, Spawn, GameStatus, Game) must not depend on environment-specific code (Main). Main depends on Game and related domain classes only.\\n- Tests use JUnit 5 (Jupiter) and reference only declared classes.\\n\\nDeterminism:\\n- SequenceSpawner consumes its sequence strictly in order for both reset() and subsequent spawns.\",\"Shared Knowledge\":\"Protocol files: pom.xml, src/main/java/Main.java (entry), and src/test/java/MainTest.java (single test) are preserved exactly. Public API and semantics:\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Direction.java: public enum Direction { LEFT, RIGHT, UP, DOWN }\\n- Used by Board.move(Direction) and Game.move(Direction).\\n\\nsrc/main/java/MoveResult.java:\\n- public final class MoveResult { public MoveResult(boolean changed, int scoreGained); public boolean changed(); public int scoreGained(); }\\n- Immutable: fields set at construction and never change. changed() indicates whether any grid cell changed. scoreGained() sums all newly created tile values from merges performed by that single move.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Spawn.java:\\n- public final class Spawn { public Spawn(int row, int col, int value); public int row(); public int col(); public int value(); }\\n- Constructor validates: 0 <= row < 4, 0 <= col < 4, value > 0 and a power of two (e.g., 2,4,8,...). Immutable.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Spawner.java:\\n- public interface Spawner { Spawn nextSpawn(); }\\n- Contract: Deterministic source. Game consumes exactly two spawns during reset() and exactly one spawn after a changed move. Implementations must not return null.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/SequenceSpawner.java:\\n- public final class SequenceSpawner implements Spawner { public SequenceSpawner(java.util.List<Spawn> seq); public Spawn nextSpawn(); public static SequenceSpawner defaultSequence(); }\\n- Holds an ordered sequence of Spawn. nextSpawn() returns sequence[index] and advances index; when reaching end, wraps to start and continues. defaultSequence() returns a deterministic spawner with a documented sequence; the first two spawns are used by Game.reset().\\n\\nsrc/main/java/GameStatus.java:\\n- public enum GameStatus { IN_PROGRESS, WON, LOST }\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Board.java:\\n- public final class Board {\\n  public Board();\\n  public void clear();\\n  public int[][] getGridCopy();\\n  public void setCell(int row, int col, int value);\\n  public MoveResult move(Direction dir);\\n  public boolean hasTileAtLeast(int value);\\n  public boolean hasAnyMoves();\\n}\\nSemantics:\\n- Board owns the authoritative 4x4 int grid. No external code may mutate it except through setCell().\\n- getGridCopy() returns a deep snapshot (new arrays). Callers must not mutate the returned arrays expecting to affect Board.\\n- setCell(row,col,value) performs bounds checks (0..3) and value validation: value == 0 or value is a positive power of two. Sets grid[row][col] accordingly.\\n- move(dir) processes each of the four lines (rows for LEFT/RIGHT, columns for UP/DOWN) independently:\\n  * Read exactly four values in movement order (LEFT: left->right; RIGHT: right->left; UP: top->bottom; DOWN: bottom->top).\\n  * Compact nonzero tiles preserving order.\\n  * Merge adjacent equal tiles at most once per adjacency (i.e., a tile participates in at most one merge). When merging two equal tiles x and x, produce 2x and add 2x to scoreGained.\\n  * After merging, compact again and fill with zeros to length four.\\n  * Write back exactly four results to the grid in the same line and movement orientation.\\n  * Overall changed flag is true if any cell differs from its previous value anywhere on the grid.\\n- hasTileAtLeast(value) returns true if any cell >= value.\\n- hasAnyMoves() returns true if any cell is zero, or any horizontal or vertical adjacent pair is equal, implying at least one legal move remains.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Game.java:\\n- public final class Game {\\n  public Game(Board board, Spawner spawner);\\n  public void reset();\\n  public MoveResult move(Direction dir);\\n  public int getScore();\\n  public GameStatus getStatus();\\n  public int[][] getGridCopy();\\n}\\nSemantics:\\n- Constructor requires non-null Board and Spawner; initializes score to 0 and status to IN_PROGRESS.\\n- reset(): calls board.clear() and applies exactly two spawns, each obtained by spawner.nextSpawn() and applied via board.setCell(). Resets score to 0 and status to IN_PROGRESS.\\n- move(dir): calls board.move(dir) once, increments internal score by result.scoreGained(). If result.changed() is true, consumes exactly one Spawn from spawner and applies it via board.setCell(). After the move attempt (even if unchanged), updates status: WON iff board.hasTileAtLeast(2048); else LOST iff !board.hasAnyMoves(); else IN_PROGRESS. Returns the MoveResult from Board.\\n- getGridCopy() proxies board.getGridCopy().\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Main.java:\\n- public final class Main { public static void main(String[] args); }\\n- Deterministic headless console demo: constructs SequenceSpawner.defaultSequence(), Board, Game; calls reset(); performs one move (e.g., Direction.LEFT); prints the 4x4 grid, current score, and status in a plain text format; exits.\\n\\nBuild & Test:\\n- pom.xml sets Java 11, includes JUnit Jupiter as test dependency, and a Surefire plugin version supporting JUnit 5. No external non-test dependencies.\\n\\nImport/Dependency rules:\\n- Board is the sole owner of the grid. All mutations go through Board.setCell().\\n- Pure domain logic (Board, MoveResult, Direction, Spawner, SequenceSpawner, Spawn, GameStatus, Game) must not depend on environment-specific code (Main). Main depends on Game and related domain classes only.\\n- Tests use JUnit 5 (Jupiter) and reference only declared classes.\\n\\nDeterminism:\\n- SequenceSpawner consumes its sequence strictly in order for both reset() and subsequent spawns.\",\"Shared Knowledge\":\"Protocol files: pom.xml, src/main/java/Main.java (entry), and src/test/java/MainTest.java (single test) are preserved exactly. Public API and semantics:\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Direction.java: public enum Direction { LEFT, RIGHT, UP, DOWN }\\n- Used by Board.move(Direction) and Game.move(Direction).\\n\\nsrc/main/java/MoveResult.java:\\n- public final class MoveResult { public MoveResult(boolean changed, int scoreGained); public boolean changed(); public int scoreGained(); }\\n- Immutable: fields set at construction and never change. changed() indicates whether any grid cell changed. scoreGained() sums all newly created tile values from merges performed by that single move.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Spawn.java:\\n- public final class Spawn { public Spawn(int row, int col, int value); public int row(); public int col(); public int value(); }\\n- Constructor validates: 0 <= row < 4, 0 <= col < 4, value > 0 and a power of two (e.g., 2,4,8,...). Immutable.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Spawner.java:\\n- public interface Spawner { Spawn nextSpawn(); }\\n- Contract: Deterministic source. Game consumes exactly two spawns during reset() and exactly one spawn after a changed move. Implementations must not return null.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/SequenceSpawner.java:\\n- public final class SequenceSpawner implements Spawner { public SequenceSpawner(java.util.List<Spawn> seq); public Spawn nextSpawn(); public static SequenceSpawner defaultSequence(); }\\n- Holds an ordered sequence of Spawn. nextSpawn() returns sequence[index] and advances index; when reaching end, wraps to start and continues. defaultSequence() returns a deterministic spawner with a documented sequence; the first two spawns are used by Game.reset().\\n\\nsrc/main/java/GameStatus.java:\\n- public enum GameStatus { IN_PROGRESS, WON, LOST }\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Board.java:\\n- public final class Board {\\n  public Board();\\n  public void clear();\\n  public int[][] getGridCopy();\\n  public void setCell(int row, int col, int value);\\n  public MoveResult move(Direction dir);\\n  public boolean hasTileAtLeast(int value);\\n  public boolean hasAnyMoves();\\n}\\nSemantics:\\n- Board owns the authoritative 4x4 int grid. No external code may mutate it except through setCell().\\n- getGridCopy() returns a deep snapshot (new arrays). Callers must not mutate the returned arrays expecting to affect Board.\\n- setCell(row,col,value) performs bounds checks (0..3) and value validation: value == 0 or value is a positive power of two. Sets grid[row][col] accordingly.\\n- move(dir) processes each of the four lines (rows for LEFT/RIGHT, columns for UP/DOWN) independently:\\n  * Read exactly four values in movement order (LEFT: left->right; RIGHT: right->left; UP: top->bottom; DOWN: bottom->top).\\n  * Compact nonzero tiles preserving order.\\n  * Merge adjacent equal tiles at most once per adjacency (i.e., a tile participates in at most one merge). When merging two equal tiles x and x, produce 2x and add 2x to scoreGained.\\n  * After merging, compact again and fill with zeros to length four.\\n  * Write back exactly four results to the grid in the same line and movement orientation.\\n  * Overall changed flag is true if any cell differs from its previous value anywhere on the grid.\\n- hasTileAtLeast(value) returns true if any cell >= value.\\n- hasAnyMoves() returns true if any cell is zero, or any horizontal or vertical adjacent pair is equal, implying at least one legal move remains.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Game.java:\\n- public final class Game {\\n  public Game(Board board, Spawner spawner);\\n  public void reset();\\n  public MoveResult move(Direction dir);\\n  public int getScore();\\n  public GameStatus getStatus();\\n  public int[][] getGridCopy();\\n}\\nSemantics:\\n- Constructor requires non-null Board and Spawner; initializes score to 0 and status to IN_PROGRESS.\\n- reset(): calls board.clear() and applies exactly two spawns, each obtained by spawner.nextSpawn() and applied via board.setCell(). Resets score to 0 and status to IN_PROGRESS.\\n- move(dir): calls board.move(dir) once, increments internal score by result.scoreGained(). If result.changed() is true, consumes exactly one Spawn from spawner and applies it via board.setCell(). After the move attempt (even if unchanged), updates status: WON iff board.hasTileAtLeast(2048); else LOST iff !board.hasAnyMoves(); else IN_PROGRESS. Returns the MoveResult from Board.\\n- getGridCopy() proxies board.getGridCopy().\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Main.java:\\n- public final class Main { public static void main(String[] args); }\\n- Deterministic headless console demo: constructs SequenceSpawner.defaultSequence(), Board, Game; calls reset(); performs one move (e.g., Direction.LEFT); prints the 4x4 grid, current score, and status in a plain text format; exits.\\n\\nBuild & Test:\\n- pom.xml sets Java 11, includes JUnit Jupiter as test dependency, and a Surefire plugin version supporting JUnit 5. No external non-test dependencies.\\n\\nImport/Dependency rules:\\n- Board is the sole owner of the grid. All mutations go through Board.setCell().\\n- Pure domain logic (Board, MoveResult, Direction, Spawner, SequenceSpawner, Spawn, GameStatus, Game) must not depend on environment-specific code (Main). Main depends on Game and related domain classes only.\\n- Tests use JUnit 5 (Jupiter) and reference only declared classes.\\n\\nDeterminism:\\n- SequenceSpawner consumes its sequence strictly in order for both reset() and subsequent spawns.\",\"Shared Knowledge\":\"Protocol files: pom.xml, src/main/java/Main.java (entry), and src/test/java/MainTest.java (single test) are preserved exactly. Immutable.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Spawner.java:\\n- public interface Spawner { Spawn nextSpawn(); }\\n- Contract: Deterministic source. Game consumes exactly two spawns during reset() and exactly one spawn after a changed move. Implementations must not return null.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/SequenceSpawner.java:\\n- public final class SequenceSpawner implements Spawner { public SequenceSpawner(java.util.List<Spawn> seq); public Spawn nextSpawn(); public static SequenceSpawner defaultSequence(); }\\n- Holds an ordered sequence of Spawn. nextSpawn() returns sequence[index] and advances index; when reaching end, wraps to start and continues. defaultSequence() returns a deterministic spawner with a documented sequence; the first two spawns are used by Game.reset().\\n\\nsrc/main/java/GameStatus.java:\\n- public enum GameStatus { IN_PROGRESS, WON, LOST }\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Board.java:\\n- public final class Board {\\n  public Board();\\n  public void clear();\\n  public int[][] getGridCopy();\\n  public void setCell(int row, int col, int value);\\n  public MoveResult move(Direction dir);\\n  public boolean hasTileAtLeast(int value);\\n  public boolean hasAnyMoves();\\n}\\nSemantics:\\n- Board owns the authoritative 4x4 int grid. No external code may mutate it except through setCell().\\n- getGridCopy() returns a deep snapshot (new arrays). Callers must not mutate the returned arrays expecting to affect Board.\\n- setCell(row,col,value) performs bounds checks (0..3) and value validation: value == 0 or value is a positive power of two. Sets grid[row][col] accordingly.\\n- move(dir) processes each of the four lines (rows for LEFT/RIGHT, columns for UP/DOWN) independently:\\n  * Read exactly four values in movement order (LEFT: left->right; RIGHT: right->left; UP: top->bottom; DOWN: bottom->top).\\n  * Compact nonzero tiles preserving order.\\n  * Merge adjacent equal tiles at most once per adjacency (i.e., a tile participates in at most one merge). When merging two equal tiles x and x, produce 2x and add 2x to scoreGained.\\n  * After merging, compact again and fill with zeros to length four.\\n  * Write back exactly four results to the grid in the same line and movement orientation.\\n  * Overall changed flag is true if any cell differs from its previous value anywhere on the grid.\\n- hasTileAtLeast(value) returns true if any cell >= value.\\n- hasAnyMoves() returns true if any cell is zero, or any horizontal or vertical adjacent pair is equal, implying at least one legal move remains.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Game.java:\\n- public final class Game {\\n  public Game(Board board, Spawner spawner);\\n  public void reset();\\n  public MoveResult move(Direction dir);\\n  public int getScore();\\n  public GameStatus getStatus();\\n  public int[][] getGridCopy();\\n}\\nSemantics:\\n- Constructor requires non-null Board and Spawner; initializes score to 0 and status to IN_PROGRESS.\\n- reset(): calls board.clear() and applies exactly two spawns, each obtained by spawner.nextSpawn() and applied via board.setCell(). Resets score to 0 and status to IN_PROGRESS.\\n- move(dir): calls board.move(dir) once, increments internal score by result.scoreGained(). If result.changed() is true, consumes exactly one Spawn from spawner and applies it via board.setCell(). After the move attempt (even if unchanged), updates status: WON iff board.hasTileAtLeast(2048); else LOST iff !board.hasAnyMoves(); else IN_PROGRESS. Returns the MoveResult from Board.\\n- getGridCopy() proxies board.getGridCopy().\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Main.java:\\n- public final class Main { public static void main(String[] args); }\\n- Deterministic headless console demo: constructs SequenceSpawner.defaultSequence(), Board, Game; calls reset(); performs one move (e.g., Direction.LEFT); prints the 4x4 grid, current score, and status in a plain text format; exits.\\n\\nBuild & Test:\\n- pom.xml sets Java 11, includes JUnit Jupiter as test dependency, and a Surefire plugin version supporting JUnit 5. No external non-test dependencies.\\n\\nImport/Dependency rules:\\n- Board is the sole owner of the grid. All mutations go through Board.setCell().\\n- Pure domain logic (Board, MoveResult, Direction, Spawner, SequenceSpawner, Spawn, GameStatus, Game) must not depend on environment-specific code (Main). Main depends on Game and related domain classes only.\\n- Tests use JUnit 5 (Jupiter) and reference only declared classes.\\n\\nDeterminism:\\n- SequenceSpawner consumes its sequence strictly in order for both reset() and subsequent spawns.\",\"Shared Knowledge\":\"Protocol files: pom.xml, src/main/java/Main.java (entry), and src/test/java/MainTest.java (single test) are preserved exactly. Immutable.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Spawner.java:\\n- public interface Spawner { Spawn nextSpawn(); }\\n- Contract: Deterministic source. Game consumes exactly two spawns during reset() and exactly one spawn after a changed move. Implementations must not return null.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/SequenceSpawner.java:\\n- public final class SequenceSpawner implements Spawner { public SequenceSpawner(java.util.List<Spawn> seq); public Spawn nextSpawn(); public static SequenceSpawner defaultSequence(); }\\n- Holds an ordered sequence of Spawn. nextSpawn() returns sequence[index] and advances index; when reaching end, wraps to start and continues. defaultSequence() returns a deterministic spawner with a documented sequence; the first two spawns are used by Game.reset().\\n\\nsrc/main/java/GameStatus.java:\\n- public enum GameStatus { IN_PROGRESS, WON, LOST }\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Board.java:\\n- public final class Board {\\n  public Board();\\n  public void clear();\\n  public int[][] getGridCopy();\\n  public void setCell(int row, int col, int value);\\n  public MoveResult move(Direction dir);\\n  public boolean hasTileAtLeast(int value);\\n  public boolean hasAnyMoves();\\n}\\nSemantics:\\n- Board owns the authoritative 4x4 int grid. No external code may mutate it except through setCell().\\n- getGridCopy() returns a deep snapshot (new arrays). Callers must not mutate the returned arrays expecting to affect Board.\\n- setCell(row,col,value) performs bounds checks (0..3) and value validation: value == 0 or value is a positive power of two. Sets grid[row][col] accordingly.\\n- move(dir) processes each of the four lines (rows for LEFT/RIGHT, columns for UP/DOWN) independently:\\n  * Read exactly four values in movement order (LEFT: left->right; RIGHT: right->left; UP: top->bottom; DOWN: bottom->top).\\n  * Compact nonzero tiles preserving order.\\n  * Merge adjacent equal tiles at most once per adjacency (i.e., a tile participates in at most one merge). When merging two equal tiles x and x, produce 2x and add 2x to scoreGained.\\n  * After merging, compact again and fill with zeros to length four.\\n  * Write back exactly four results to the grid in the same line and movement orientation.\\n  * Overall changed flag is true if any cell differs from its previous value anywhere on the grid.\\n- hasTileAtLeast(value) returns true if any cell >= value.\\n- hasAnyMoves() returns true if any cell is zero, or any horizontal or vertical adjacent pair is equal, implying at least one legal move remains.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Game.java:\\n- public final class Game {\\n  public Game(Board board, Spawner spawner);\\n  public void reset();\\n  public MoveResult move(Direction dir);\\n  public int getScore();\\n  public GameStatus getStatus();\\n  public int[][] getGridCopy();\\n}\\nSemantics:\\n- Constructor requires non-null Board and Spawner; initializes score to 0 and status to IN_PROGRESS.\\n- reset(): calls board.clear() and applies exactly two spawns, each obtained by spawner.nextSpawn() and applied via board.setCell(). Resets score to 0 and status to IN_PROGRESS.\\n- move(dir): calls board.move(dir) once, increments internal score by result.scoreGained(). If result.changed() is true, consumes exactly one Spawn from spawner and applies it via board.setCell(). After the move attempt (even if unchanged), updates status: WON iff board.hasTileAtLeast(2048); else LOST iff !board.hasAnyMoves(); else IN_PROGRESS. Returns the MoveResult from Board.\\n- getGridCopy() proxies board.getGridCopy().\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Main.java:\\n- public final class Main { public static void main(String[] args); }\\n- Deterministic headless console demo: constructs SequenceSpawner.defaultSequence(), Board, Game; calls reset(); performs one move (e.g., Direction.LEFT); prints the 4x4 grid, current score, and status in a plain text format; exits.\\n\\nBuild & Test:\\n- pom.xml sets Java 11, includes JUnit Jupiter as test dependency, and a Surefire plugin version supporting JUnit 5. No external non-test dependencies.\\n\\nImport/Dependency rules:\\n- Board is the sole owner of the grid. All mutations go through Board.setCell().\\n- Pure domain logic (Board, MoveResult, Direction, Spawner, SequenceSpawner, Spawn, GameStatus, Game) must not depend on environment-specific code (Main). Main depends on Game and related domain classes only.\\n- Tests use JUnit 5 (Jupiter) and reference only declared classes.\\n\\nDeterminism:\\n- SequenceSpawner consumes its sequence strictly in order for both reset() and subsequent spawns.\",\"Shared Knowledge\":\"Protocol files: pom.xml, src/main/java/Main.java (entry), and src/test/java/MainTest.java (single test) are preserved exactly. Public API and semantics:\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Direction.java: public enum Direction { LEFT, RIGHT, UP, DOWN }\\n- Used by Board.move(Direction) and Game.move(Direction).\\n\\nsrc/main/java/MoveResult.java:\\n- public final class MoveResult { public MoveResult(boolean changed, int scoreGained); public boolean changed(); public int scoreGained(); }\\n- Immutable: fields set at construction and never change. changed() indicates whether any grid cell changed. scoreGained() sums all newly created tile values from merges performed by that single move.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Spawn.java:\\n- public final class Spawn { public Spawn(int row, int col, int value); public int row(); public int col(); public int value(); }\\n- Constructor validates: 0 <= row < 4, 0 <= col < 4, value > 0 and a power of two (e.g., 2,4,8,...). Immutable.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Spawner.java:\\n- public interface Spawner { Spawn nextSpawn(); }\\n- Contract: Deterministic source. Game consumes exactly two spawns during reset() and exactly one spawn after a changed move. Implementations must not return null.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/SequenceSpawner.java:\\n- public final class SequenceSpawner implements Spawner { public SequenceSpawner(java.util.List<Spawn> seq); public Spawn nextSpawn(); public static SequenceSpawner defaultSequence(); }\\n- Holds an ordered sequence of Spawn. nextSpawn() returns sequence[index] and advances index; when reaching end, wraps to start and continues. defaultSequence() returns a deterministic spawner with a documented sequence; the first two spawns are used by Game.reset().\\n\\nsrc/main/java/GameStatus.java:\\n- public enum GameStatus { IN_PROGRESS, WON, LOST }\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Board.java:\\n- public final class Board {\\n  public Board();\\n  public void clear();\\n  public int[][] getGridCopy();\\n  public void setCell(int row, int col, int value);\\n  public MoveResult move(Direction dir);\\n  public boolean hasTileAtLeast(int value);\\n  public boolean hasAnyMoves();\\n}\\nSemantics:\\n- Board owns the authoritative 4x4 int grid. No external code may mutate it except through setCell().\\n- getGridCopy() returns a deep snapshot (new arrays). Callers must not mutate the returned arrays expecting to affect Board.\\n- setCell(row,col,value) performs bounds checks (0..3) and value validation: value == 0 or value is a positive power of two. Sets grid[row][col] accordingly.\\n- move(dir) processes each of the four lines (rows for LEFT/RIGHT, columns for UP/DOWN) independently:\\n  * Read exactly four values in movement order (LEFT: left->right; RIGHT: right->left; UP: top->bottom; DOWN: bottom->top).\\n  * Compact nonzero tiles preserving order.\\n  * Merge adjacent equal tiles at most once per adjacency (i.e., a tile participates in at most one merge). When merging two equal tiles x and x, produce 2x and add 2x to scoreGained.\\n  * After merging, compact again and fill with zeros to length four.\\n  * Write back exactly four results to the grid in the same line and movement orientation.\\n  * Overall changed flag is true if any cell differs from its previous value anywhere on the grid.\\n- hasTileAtLeast(value) returns true if any cell >= value.\\n- hasAnyMoves() returns true if any cell is zero, or any horizontal or vertical adjacent pair is equal, implying at least one legal move remains.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Game.java:\\n- public final class Game {\\n  public Game(Board board, Spawner spawner);\\n  public void reset();\\n  public MoveResult move(Direction dir);\\n  public int getScore();\\n  public GameStatus getStatus();\\n  public int[][] getGridCopy();\\n}\\nSemantics:\\n- Constructor requires non-null Board and Spawner; initializes score to 0 and status to IN_PROGRESS.\\n- reset(): calls board.clear() and applies exactly two spawns, each obtained by spawner.nextSpawn() and applied via board.setCell(). Resets score to 0 and status to IN_PROGRESS.\\n- move(dir): calls board.move(dir) once, increments internal score by result.scoreGained(). If result.changed() is true, consumes exactly one Spawn from spawner and applies it via board.setCell(). After the move attempt (even if unchanged), updates status: WON iff board.hasTileAtLeast(2048); else LOST iff !board.hasAnyMoves(); else IN_PROGRESS. Returns the MoveResult from Board.\\n- getGridCopy() proxies board.getGridCopy().\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Main.java:\\n- public final class Main { public static void main(String[] args); }\\n- Deterministic headless console demo: constructs SequenceSpawner.defaultSequence(), Board, Game; calls reset(); performs one move (e.g., Direction.LEFT); prints the 4x4 grid, current score, and status in a plain text format; exits.\\n\\nBuild & Test:\\n- pom.xml sets Java 11, includes JUnit Jupiter as test dependency, and a Surefire plugin version supporting JUnit 5. No external non-test dependencies.\\n\\nImport/Dependency rules:\\n- Board is the sole owner of the grid. All mutations go through Board.setCell().\\n- Pure domain logic (Board, MoveResult, Direction, Spawner, SequenceSpawner, Spawn, GameStatus, Game) must not depend on environment-specific code (Main). Main depends on Game and related domain classes only.\\n- Tests use JUnit 5 (Jupiter) and reference only declared classes.\\n\\nDeterminism:\\n- SequenceSpawner consumes its sequence strictly in order for both reset() and subsequent spawns.\",\"Shared Knowledge\":\"Protocol files: pom.xml, src/main/java/Main.java (entry), and src/test/java/MainTest.java (single test) are preserved exactly. Game consumes exactly two spawns during reset() and exactly one spawn after a changed move. Implementations must not return null.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/SequenceSpawner.java:\\n- public final class SequenceSpawner implements Spawner { public SequenceSpawner(java.util.List<Spawn> seq); public Spawn nextSpawn(); public static SequenceSpawner defaultSequence(); }\\n- Holds an ordered sequence of Spawn. nextSpawn() returns sequence[index] and advances index; when reaching end, wraps to start and continues. defaultSequence() returns a deterministic spawner with a documented sequence; the first two spawns are used by Game.reset().\\n\\nsrc/main/java/GameStatus.java:\\n- public enum GameStatus { IN_PROGRESS, WON, LOST }\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Board.java:\\n- public final class Board {\\n  public Board();\\n  public void clear();\\n  public int[][] getGridCopy();\\n  public void setCell(int row, int col, int value);\\n  public MoveResult move(Direction dir);\\n  public boolean hasTileAtLeast(int value);\\n  public boolean hasAnyMoves();\\n}\\nSemantics:\\n- Board owns the authoritative 4x4 int grid. No external code may mutate it except through setCell().\\n- getGridCopy() returns a deep snapshot (new arrays). Callers must not mutate the returned arrays expecting to affect Board.\\n- setCell(row,col,value) performs bounds checks (0..3) and value validation: value == 0 or value is a positive power of two. Sets grid[row][col] accordingly.\\n- move(dir) processes each of the four lines (rows for LEFT/RIGHT, columns for UP/DOWN) independently:\\n  * Read exactly four values in movement order (LEFT: left->right; RIGHT: right->left; UP: top->bottom; DOWN: bottom->top).\\n  * Compact nonzero tiles preserving order.\\n  * Merge adjacent equal tiles at most once per adjacency (i.e., a tile participates in at most one merge). When merging two equal tiles x and x, produce 2x and add 2x to scoreGained.\\n  * After merging, compact again and fill with zeros to length four.\\n  * Write back exactly four results to the grid in the same line and movement orientation.\\n  * Overall changed flag is true if any cell differs from its previous value anywhere on the grid.\\n- hasTileAtLeast(value) returns true if any cell >= value.\\n- hasAnyMoves() returns true if any cell is zero, or any horizontal or vertical adjacent pair is equal, implying at least one legal move remains.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Game.java:\\n- public final class Game {\\n  public Game(Board board, Spawner spawner);\\n  public void reset();\\n  public MoveResult move(Direction dir);\\n  public int getScore();\\n  public GameStatus getStatus();\\n  public int[][] getGridCopy();\\n}\\nSemantics:\\n- Constructor requires non-null Board and Spawner; initializes score to 0 and status to IN_PROGRESS.\\n- reset(): calls board.clear() and applies exactly two spawns, each obtained by spawner.nextSpawn() and applied via board.setCell(). Resets score to 0 and status to IN_PROGRESS.\\n- move(dir): calls board.move(dir) once, increments internal score by result.scoreGained(). If result.changed() is true, consumes exactly one Spawn from spawner and applies it via board.setCell(). After the move attempt (even if unchanged), updates status: WON iff board.hasTileAtLeast(2048); else LOST iff !board.hasAnyMoves(); else IN_PROGRESS. Returns the MoveResult from Board.\\n- getGridCopy() proxies board.getGridCopy().\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Main.java:\\n- public final class Main { public static void main(String[] args); }\\n- Deterministic headless console demo: constructs SequenceSpawner.defaultSequence(), Board, Game; calls reset(); performs one move (e.g., Direction.LEFT); prints the 4x4 grid, current score, and status in a plain text format; exits.\\n\\nBuild & Test:\\n- pom.xml sets Java 11, includes JUnit Jupiter as test dependency, and a Surefire plugin version supporting JUnit 5. Generate a complete medium-size Java 11 repository architecture for: 2048 game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: pom.xml
- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.


Project-specific Java correctness contract:
- Board is the sole owner of one authoritative 4x4 int grid; getGridCopy() returns a deep read-only snapshot, so Game and spawners must never try to mutate the board through getGridCopy()
- declare one exact mutation API void setCell(int row, int col, int value) with bounds checks and 0-or-power-of-two validation, and use it consistently for deterministic setup and applying every Spawn; do not invent setGridValue, placeTile, setTile, or aliases
- declare boolean hasTileAtLeast(int value) on Board and use that exact name for win detection; do not invent hasValueAtLeast or aliases
- declare a simple immutable MoveResult with exact accessors boolean changed() and int scoreGained(); Board.move(Direction) returns it, and Game must use these methods rather than fields
- Board.move must implement each row/column by reading exactly four values in movement order, compacting nonzero values, merging one equal adjacent pair at most once, compacting/filling with zero, writing all four results back to the authoritative grid, and summing each newly merged tile into scoreGained; forbid generic multi-delta helpers with unused or ambiguous row/column parameters
- Game.move(Direction) calls Board.move once, adds scoreGained, and spawns exactly one tile only when changed() is true; apply the Spawn via Board.setCell, never via a copied array
- Game must update status after every move attempt, including an unchanged move: WON iff Board.hasTileAtLeast(2048), otherwise LOST iff !Board.hasAnyMoves(), otherwise IN_PROGRESS
- initialization/reset must clear the authoritative Board and apply exactly two spawns through Board.setCell; a deterministic SequenceSpawner must consume its documented sequence in order
- keep MainTest to 2--4 concise deterministic tests using only the canonical methods; do not assert mutations made to arrays returned by getGridCopy()
- repeat the exact getGridCopy immutability, setCell, hasTileAtLeast, MoveResult, line-merge, spawn-on-change, and status-transition rules in Full API specification, Logic Analysis, Shared Knowledge, and every affected implementation task; vague descriptions are insufficient


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 7 repository files
- about 33 functions or methods
- about 650 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- 4x4 board
- left right up and down moves
- single-merge-per-move rule
- score accumulation
- deterministic tile spawning
- win loss and reset states

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix

Generate a complete medium-size Java 11 repository architecture for: 2048 game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: pom.xml
- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.


Project-specific Java correctness contract:
- Board is the sole owner of one authoritative 4x4 int grid; getGridCopy() returns a deep read-only snapshot, so Game and spawners must never try to mutate the board through getGridCopy()
- declare one exact mutation API void setCell(int row, int col, int value) with bounds checks and 0-or-power-of-two validation, and use it consistently for deterministic setup and applying every Spawn; do not invent setGridValue, placeTile, setTile, or aliases
- declare boolean hasTileAtLeast(int value) on Board and use that exact name for win detection; do not invent hasValueAtLeast or aliases
- declare a simple immutable MoveResult with exact accessors boolean changed() and int scoreGained(); Board.move(Direction) returns it, and Game must use these methods rather than fields
- Board.move must implement each row/column by reading exactly four values in movement order, compacting nonzero values, merging one equal adjacent pair at most once, compacting/filling with zero, writing all four results back to the authoritative grid, and summing each newly merged tile into scoreGained; forbid generic multi-delta helpers with unused or ambiguous row/column parameters
- Game.move(Direction) calls Board.move once, adds scoreGained, and spawns exactly one tile only when changed() is true; apply the Spawn via Board.setCell, never via a copied array
- Game must update status after every move attempt, including an unchanged move: WON iff Board.hasTileAtLeast(2048), otherwise LOST iff !Board.hasAnyMoves(), otherwise IN_PROGRESS
- initialization/reset must clear the authoritative Board and apply exactly two spawns through Board.setCell; a deterministic SequenceSpawner must consume its documented sequence in order
- keep MainTest to 2--4 concise deterministic tests using only the canonical methods; do not assert mutations made to arrays returned by getGridCopy()
- repeat the exact getGridCopy immutability, setCell, hasTileAtLeast, MoveResult, line-merge, spawn-on-change, and status-transition rules in Full API specification, Logic Analysis, Shared Knowledge, and every affected implementation task; vague descriptions are insufficient


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 7 repository files
- about 33 functions or methods
- about 650 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- 4x4 board
- left right up and down moves
- single-merge-per-move rule
- score accumulation
- deterministic tile spawning
- win loss and reset states

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Generate a complete medium-size Java 11 repository architecture for: 2048 game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: pom.xml
- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.


Project-specific Java correctness contract:
- Board is the sole owner of one authoritative 4x4 int grid; getGridCopy() returns a deep read-only snapshot, so Game and spawners must never try to mutate the board through getGridCopy()
- declare one exact mutation API void setCell(int row, int col, int value) with bounds checks and 0-or-power-of-two validation, and use it consistently for deterministic setup and applying every Spawn; do not invent setGridValue, placeTile, setTile, or aliases
- declare boolean hasTileAtLeast(int value) on Board and use that exact name for win detection; do not invent hasValueAtLeast or aliases
- declare a simple immutable MoveResult with exact accessors boolean changed() and int scoreGained(); Board.move(Direction) returns it, and Game must use these methods rather than fields
- Board.move must implement each row/column by reading exactly four values in movement order, compacting nonzero values, merging one equal adjacent pair at most once, compacting/filling with zero, writing all four results back to the authoritative grid, and summing each newly merged tile into scoreGained; forbid generic multi-delta helpers with unused or ambiguous row/column parameters
- Game.move(Direction) calls Board.move once, adds scoreGained, and spawns exactly one tile only when changed() is true; apply the Spawn via Board.setCell, never via a copied array
- Game must update status after every move attempt, including an unchanged move: WON iff Board.hasTileAtLeast(2048), otherwise LOST iff !Board.hasAnyMoves(), otherwise IN_PROGRESS
- initialization/reset must clear the authoritative Board and apply exactly two spawns through Board.setCell; a deterministic SequenceSpawner must consume its documented sequence in order
- keep MainTest to 2--4 concise deterministic tests using only the canonical methods; do not assert mutations made to arrays returned by getGridCopy()
- repeat the exact getGridCopy immutability, setCell, hasTileAtLeast, MoveResult, line-merge, spawn-on-change, and status-transition rules in Full API specification, Logic Analysis, Shared Knowledge, and every affected implementation task; vague descriptions are insufficient

- about 7 repository files
- about 33 functions or methods
- about 650 lines of code

- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- 4x4 board
- left right up and down moves
- single-merge-per-move rule
- score accumulation
- deterministic tile spawning
- win loss and reset states

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction

- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
